pr_body:
The main objective of this PR is to address the linked issue below. The main changes in this PR include:
- `LocalHealthMonitor`: to allow for a more "scalable" setup, I added the abstract class `HealthCheck<T>`, which represents a health check that will be performed on every node, and made `LocalHealthMonitor` work with a list of `HealthCheck`s. This reduces future effort to add new health checks.
  - Also extracted `DiskCheck` to a separate class/file.
  - And added `RepositoriesCheck` for this new feature.
- `RepositoryIntegrityHealthIndicatorService`: refactored this class to do a more extensive analysis of the repository health in the cluster.
- Field additions, new `TransportVersion`, constructor updates, etc.

Fixes #103784
pr_title: Extend `repository_integrity` health indicator for unknown and invalid repos

I think we can explain here how it helps us. For example:

> We use the previous observed value to verify that no other concurrent process has updated the health check's value.

Food for thought.... I just realise that we might have a race here, can you think along with me on the following scenario and its implications:

- Last reported value was null
- there is new health node
- New run starts the update process and records previous value `null`
- health node/master change
- new reported value is `null`
- Run sees null and considers that it's ok to update the value.... 

What do you think?

Hm I think you might be right. The only workaround I can think of right now is to have some kind of ref counter that increments every time we send a request, so we can be 100% sure there weren't any other requests sent while waiting for the response of the first request. That way, the last step you mentioned won't be executed, as the ref counter doesn't match, so we're not updating any `lastReportedValue`s as we know there's already another request on its way. I think that implementation should also be doable, what do you think?
Yes, I was thinking something like that too. A versioned "last value". We can also open an issue and address it in a follow up PR.
